findings.title: Comma-coalesced binary gRPC metadata still attributes splitting to Tonic

evidence.observation: Separate HTTP wire and decoded gRPC projections now exist, but the text still says comma-coalesced binary values are accepted by Tonic and projected individually without specifying Adapter splitting.
Preserved source inspection reports MetadataMap::from_headers wraps HeaderMap; MetadataValue::to_bytes decodes the whole value without comma splitting.

findings.impact: The mapping would leave a valid coalesced binary field to a decoder that does not split it, causing failure or divergent metadata semantics.
findings.required_resolution: Specify bounded Rust Adapter splitting of coalesced -bin field values, permitted ASCII OWS trimming, individual validation and Tonic decoding per segment, original order and repeated-entry preservation, empty/malformed rules, aggregate limits and split/decode scratch reservation. Keep the wire HTTP block intact and require no managed base64 decode.
findings.review_limit: This reviewer independently inspected the current design and preserved source finding; no new upstream runtime experiment was run.

findings.title: Successful raw response lacks a guaranteed response_finish before cleanup

evidence.observation: LIFO failure-isolated cleanup is specified, but no dispatcher rule completes an unfinished successful HTTP response before OnCompleted and scope release.
The MapRaw upload handler sets StatusCode201 and returns without CompleteAsync.

findings.impact: A normal documented handler can finish application dispatch without an admitted response_finish operation, leaving output incomplete and retirement ambiguous.
findings.required_resolution: For successful HTTP MapRaw, generated void/Task, custom result and middleware short-circuit paths, await the one idempotent CompleteAsync/response_finish if not already completed before OnCompleted/disposal/dispatch_complete. Preserve selected status and headers; untouched response is empty200. Failure must follow the existing redacted precommit error or postcommit abort path, and protocol-owned output must use its own terminal operation.

findings.title: gRPC RequestContext exposure lacks explicit raw HTTP and filter restrictions

evidence.observation: GrpcCallContext exposes the ordinary RequestContext; typed protocol framing exists but raw body/response/OnStarting/filter restrictions are absent.
MCP has a concrete single-ticket pre-parse gate, continuation, scope and retirement contract, but remaining gRPC restrictions and complete cross-protocol policy need to agree.

findings.impact: Normal middleware or a gRPC handler can apparently consume transport body bytes or commit an HTTP response outside Tonic, corrupting protocol framing; inherited ServerFilter has no typed gRPC result to wrap.
findings.required_resolution: Explicitly permit safe metadata, services, identity, Items, cancellation/abort and lifecycle completion/disposal access. Reject gRPC raw Request.Body/ReadChunk/ReadJson/GetTrailers and response status/header/trailer/body/Start/Write/Flush/Complete/OnStarting mutation; use only typed gRPC metadata/status/output paths. Reject endpoint/inherited ServerFilter at route freeze. Define auth/policy denial through gRPC Unauthenticated/PermissionDenied framing. Reconcile declarations, type policies and D19. Preserve MCP AwaitingGate managed HTTP denial exception and post-Allow native ownership.
findings.already_rechecked: The main MCP gate defect is repaired in current design: all native automatic methods pass kind2 gate; kind3 uses same ticket with one take/scope/auth chain; nested managed invocation lease and native retirement prevent early release. This is a design review, not executed cross-language gate evidence.

findings.title: Retained inbound chunks can consume capacity required by an awaited response

evidence.observation: The per-request native retained-byte cap may be filled by retained BodyChunk owners; a positive output write waits for that same request/global byte capacity. The existing managed/native acquisition order does not address same-side retained input owners.

findings.counterexample: With the default4MiB per-request native cap and32KiB chunks plus a route body override, retain128 complete chunks, then await positive Response.WriteAsync before disposing them in finally. Output cannot gain byte credit until the awaiting handler releases its chunks; only deadline/cancellation breaks the wait. Equivalent global exhaustion can occur across requests.
findings.impact: A currently admitted pattern has a deadline-bounded liveness failure. This is a semantic design gap, not an executed product failure or evidence of unbounded deadlock.
findings.required_resolution: Choose exact all-or-none nonwaiting native payload credit failure on both read/write capacity exhaustion, clearly separate queue/network flow-control waiting, and unwind partial grants; alternatively specify protected directional/request headroom plus globally atomic admission. Per-request minimum alone is insufficient. Charge actual backing capacities and preserve owned-chunk retirement. Require B16 boundary/global/cancellation/untaken-owner witnesses. Do not use a retry loop or timeout to claim progress.
